newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firmer on high money market rates.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firmer on high money market rates.

text.p: The Mexican peso stretched midday strength at the close on Monday on what dealers said was demand for pesos in order to take advantage of high rates payable in the secondary money market.
"Late strength was mainly due to long (dollar) positions in the market and the fact high (secondary) rates made it expensive to hold them," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed trade 1.4 centavos firmer at 7.9320/7.9350 and 7.9280/7.9300 per dollar, respectively.
Dealers said some players may even have gone short on dollars due to market predictions the Federal Open Market Committee will not raise U.S. interest rates at its meeting on Wednesday.
"I don't think U.S. (base) rates will come under pressure. It is practically a fact they won't raise rates," the dealer added.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 1.0 centavo firmer at 7.9420/7.9450 per dollar.
Dealers said they awaited reaction on the U.S. bond market to data due on Tuesday from the National Association of Purchasing Managers.
